## Overview

The between/within split extended to **receptive vocabulary** (#553): pooled across all four waves, how does receptive-vocabulary level go with word-reading level, and does that association live between children or within a child's own movement? The transition counterpart is `lrp-rli-mech-056` (R → W given the period-start word-reading score); this model has no own-baseline term.

The exposure is split into its child mean and the deviation from it. The adjustment set mirrors `mech-056` minus the own baseline: hearing and phonological memory (each with a missing-indicator), the **same-wave standardised logit of taught receptive vocabulary** as a skill adjuster (`gamma_TR` — a contemporaneous, possibly post-treatment level, so an adjusted association), the t1 block-design ability proxy and linear age. Session dose (`attend`) is omitted as in `pl-001`. Rows are kept only when the outcome, the exposure and the skill adjuster are observed at the wave; the dropped count is reported.

## Model

$$
\eta = \alpha_{\text{wave}} + \beta_G G
  + \beta_{\text{between}}\bar z_i + \beta_{\text{within}}(z_{it} - \bar z_i)
  + \gamma_A z(A) + \sum_c \gamma_c z(c) + \gamma_{\mathrm{TR}} z_{\mathrm{TR},it} + u_{\text{child}}
$$

where $z_{it}$ is the standardised exposure logit at wave $t$, $\bar z_i$ its
child mean, and $z_{\mathrm{TR},it}$ the standardised same-wave logit of taught
receptive vocabulary. There is deliberately no own-baseline term.
